title: Mukesh Kumar joins Nottinghamshire for title-chasing County Championship run-in
excerpt: India seamer Mukesh Kumar has signed with Nottinghamshire for the final two games of the 2026 County Championship season, with the club sitting four points behind leaders Somerset in the Division One title race.
body:
• Mukesh Kumar has signed with Nottinghamshire for the final two matches of the 2026 County Championship season.
  • The India seamer will face Sussex at Hove from September 15 and Yorkshire at Trent Bridge from September 24.
  • Nottinghamshire sit second in Division One, four points behind leaders Somerset with two rounds left to play.
  • The stint is Kumar's first experience of English domestic cricket, arriving straight from the Duleep Trophy final.

Nottinghamshire have signed India fast bowler Mukesh Kumar for the last two matches of the 2026 County Championship season, drafting in the 32-year-old seamer for a title run-in that could decide Division One. The county, sitting second in the table and four points behind leaders Somerset with two rounds of fixtures remaining, announced the deal on Monday.

Kumar will play against Sussex at Hove from Tuesday, September 15, before finishing with a home fixture against Yorkshire at Trent Bridge starting September 24, according to ESPNcricinfo. It is the first time in his career that the Bengal right-armer will represent a domestic side outside India.

Context & Background

Kumar arrives in England with 233 first-class wickets at an average of 21.79, including ten five-wicket hauls and one ten-wicket match haul, as listed by the club. His career-best figures of 10 for 50 came for Bengal against his home state of Bihar in a Ranji Trophy match in February 2024. At the international level, he has 26 caps for India across all formats, including three Tests, with 32 wickets in total.

His most eye-catching Test performance came in his second appearance, in January 2024, when he claimed 2 for 0 in the first innings as South Africa were bowled out for 55 in Cape Town, a match India won by seven wickets. Kumar has also featured for Delhi Capitals in each of the past four editions of the IPL.

He lands at Trent Bridge in competitive rhythm. Only days before the signing, Kumar took 3 for 62 in the Duleep Trophy final as East Zone defeated South Zone by virtue of a first-innings lead to lift the title for the first time in 14 years.

"We’re really excited to get Mukesh over at what is a crucial time of the season. It’s fantastic for us to get a player who’s match-ready and in full competitive mode ahead of two big games for the club."

— Peter Moores, Nottinghamshire head coach

Impact & Analysis

For Nottinghamshire, the logic of the move is plain. With two games left and Somerset only four points ahead, the club is plugging an experienced, battle-tested seamer into a bowling attack for the sharp end of the season. Moores pointed directly to Kumar's recent workload as the attraction: he comes straight from a high-stakes domestic final rather than from a layoff.

"He comes straight off the back of a really competitive game in the Duleep Trophy Final, in which he was on the winning team and played a pivotal role in securing the win for East Zone," Moores said. "Mukesh’s quality as a bowler is not in question, knowing how hard it is to compete to play in the Indian team."

Kumar himself sounded eager for the challenge of English conditions, a test every Indian seamer's career is eventually measured by. "I can’t wait to arrive in England and test myself in county cricket," he said in a club statement. "I want to contribute as much as I can while I am here to help Nottinghamshire to success, and I am looking forward to working with the coaches and my new team-mates. Coming to England is always a good challenge, and I am excited by the chance to play for a new team in new conditions."

Diaspora Angle

Kumar is not the first Indian connection at Trent Bridge this cycle: Nottinghamshire signed Ishan Kishan as an overseas player for 2025, and both cricketers hail from Bihar. For British Asian cricket fans, county sides have become a familiar late-summer window onto Indian talent. Trent Bridge, in a city with one of England's largest South Asian communities, will see an India international wearing the green and gold for two games that actually matter — a title race, not a mid-table dead rubber.

What’s Next

The immediate test is Hove, starting Tuesday. Sussex away is no gentle introduction to the County Championship, and how quickly Kumar adapts his lengths to the Dukes ball and September English pitches will decide whether Nottinghamshire's gamble pays off in the points column. If Notts lift the title, the seamer who flew in for two games will have played his part; either way, a strong showing puts his name back in the conversation for India's overseas tours. After Yorkshire, Kumar returns to India with two weeks of English first-class cricket banked — experience money cannot buy for an Indian seamer eyeing the national side's next foreign assignment.

nri_angle: An India international in a Division One title race gives British Asian cricket fans — and the large South Asian community around Trent Bridge — a live stake in the English county season's closing act.
